newsitem.title: DENMARK: Gazprom studying northern Europe gas pipeline plan.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom studying northern Europe gas pipeline plan.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, June 11, Reuter - Plans by Gazprom to build a new export pipeline through Finland, Sweden and Denmark are still at the feasibility stage, Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev said on Wednesday.
He also expressed regret that Norway had sold gas to the Czech republic and taken market share from Russia.
Asked how he felt about competition between Norway and Russia, Vyakhirev replied: "I don't like the idea but I can't avoid it."
He added that both Russia and Norway negotiated with the Czech Republic, which was actively looking to diversify its sources of supply away from Russia.
"We were not the ones," he said. "I can do nothing about it. I don't like it but that's life."

Gazprom has commissioned a feasibility study, with partner Neste of Finland, to decide whether to go ahead with a new export link through Finland, Sweden and Denmark, feeding all those markets and allowing the possibility of exports into central Europe.
Asked if he was already in discussions with potential customers in the region, Vyakhirev replied that Russia's export corridor through Ukraine was already overloaded.
"So we will look at the possibility of building another line on the basis of existing contracts," he said, adding that the company was looking to sell more gas abroad.
